record.context_brief: Hurwitz stability of higher-order Toeplitz determinants
record.original_question: Suppose {f_k}_{k=0}^n is a finite Polya frequency sequence of order d >= r. Must the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant polynomial P_n^r(z) be Hurwitz stable, meaning that all of its zeros lie in the open left half-plane?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3. Suppose {fk}_k=0^n is a finite Polya frequency sequence of order d >= r. Then the polynomial P_n^r(z) is Hurwitz stable (all its zeros lie on the open left half-plane). In particular, it has positive coefficients.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{f_k\}_{k=0}^n$ be a finite sequence of nonnegative real numbers. For an integer $d\ge 1$, the sequence is called a Pólya frequency sequence of order $d$ (briefly, $\mathrm{PF}_d$) if every minor of order at most $d$ of the (one-sided) infinite Toeplitz matrix
$$T(f) = \big(f_{i-j}\big)_{i,j\ge 0}, \qquad f_k := 0 \text{ for } k<0 \text{ or } k>n,$$
is nonnegative.

For an integer $r\ge 1$, define the higher-order Toeplitz-determinant polynomial
$$P_n^r(z) \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{n} D_k^{(r)}\, z^k,$$
where $D_k^{(r)}$ denotes the determinant of the $r\times r$ Toeplitz matrix
$$D_k^{(r)} \;=\; \det\!\big(f_{k + i - j}\big)_{1\le i,j\le r},$$
with the convention that $f_m = 0$ when $m<0$ or $m>n$.

A polynomial with real coefficients is said to be Hurwitz stable if all of its complex zeros lie in the open left half-plane $\{z\in\mathbb{C} : \Re(z) < 0\}$.

Prove or disprove: whenever $\{f_k\}_{k=0}^n$ is a finite Pólya frequency sequence of order $d \ge r$, the polynomial $P_n^r(z)$ is Hurwitz stable (and in particular has all positive coefficients).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as a conjecture in a 2023 collection of open problems on polynomials and their zero distributions. A web search did not surface a published proof or counterexample; related recent work (e.g., on PF order thresholds for Toeplitz determinants) discusses adjacent phenomena but does not resolve this stability conjecture. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on polynomials, their zero distribution and related questions: 2023
status_evidence.snippet: Collects open problems presented at the 'Hausdorff Geometry of Polynomials' workshop held on July 10-14, 2023 in Sofia, Bulgaria.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is presented in a 2023 collection of open problems, indicating it was unresolved at that time.

status_evidence.title: On the Pólya Frequency Order of the de Bruijn Newman Kernel. Certified Failure at Order Five and the Toeplitz Threshold Phenomenon
status_evidence.snippet: Toeplitz determinants are certified positive for all lower orders by interval arithmetic.
status_evidence.claim: Recent related work studies higher-order Toeplitz determinants and PF orders but does not resolve the Hurwitz stability conjecture.
